1Outcome

Each participant is supported to understand the terms and conditions that apply to their specialist disability accommodation dwelling and the associated service and/or tenancy agreements.

2Quality indicators

(1)

Work is undertaken with each participant to develop a written service agreement that meets the requirements of the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation Conditions) Rules 2018, and any applicable state or territory residential tenancy legislation.

Our commitment: Policy C1, Policy C2, Policy C14. Proof: REG-SDA-02.

(2)

In the absence of any applicable state or territory residential tenancy legislation, written service agreements should deal with the following matters:

  1. (a)specify the rent that must be paid by the participant and the method and timing of making rental payments and arrangements for the issuance of rental payment receipts;
  2. (b)specify the value and management arrangements in relation to any bond that is required from the participant;
  3. (c)if applicable, specify any board payments that have been agreed with the participant, what the board payments will cover and the method and timing of making the board payments;
  4. (e)specify the minimum period of notice that will be given by the provider before the provider increases the amount of rent or board (where applicable) payable by the participant;
  5. (f)specify:
    1. (i)the name, telephone number and address of the provider’s agent (if any) and the responsibilities of the agent; or
    2. (ii)if the provider does not have an agent, the address and telephone number, of the provider;
  6. (g)require the provider to notify the participant in writing within 5 business days of any change during the agreement of the matters provided for in paragraph (f), unless applicable state or territory law stipulates an alternative notice period;
  7. (h)specify the commencement date of the agreement, the duration of the agreement, and the manner in which the agreement can be extended;
  8. (j)specify the circumstances in which the agreement can be terminated by either the participant or the provider;
  9. (k)require the provider to give the participant a minimum of 90 days’ notice before the participant is required to vacate the premises, unless shorter notice is required to address risks of harm to the participant or others;
  10. (l)explain the process for requesting repairs or maintenance to be undertaken.

Our commitment: Policy C3, Policy C4, Policy C5, Policy C6, Policy C7, Policy C8, Policy C9.

(3)

The agreement establishes expectations, explains the responsibilities of the specialist disability accommodation provider in relation to the dwelling, and specifies the rights and responsibilities of the participant in accessing the dwelling.

Our commitment: Policy C10.

(4)

The agreement includes information about dwelling safety features, including fire alarms and building evacuation procedures, and how this information will be communicated to other providers who deliver supported independent living to each participant in the dwelling.

Our commitment: Policy C11. Proof: REG-SDA-01.

(5)

Each participant is supported to understand the agreement, including any conditions, by using the language, mode of communication and terms which that participant is most likely to understand.

Our commitment: Policy C12.

(6)

Each participant receives a copy of their agreement signed by the participant and the provider. Where this is not practicable, a record is made detailing the circumstances in which the participant did not receive a copy of their agreement.

Our commitment: Policy C13, Policy C14. Proof: REG-SDA-02.

1Purpose

This policy sets out what [Provider name] commits to when it gives a participant a written for their dwelling. It is for participants, their supporters, our workers and the people who check our work.

2Applies to

  • Everyone who works for [Provider name], including an who acts for us on a dwelling.
  • Every participant who lives in, or has accepted a place in, an SDA dwelling we have enrolled.
  • Every agreement about the dwelling: the first agreement, each change, each review and the ending.
  • The home only. The supports a participant gets, even from us, are under POL-SUP-03 Service Agreements with Participants Policy and AGR-SUP-01 Service Agreement Template.
  • Not a participant who provides SDA to themselves. They need no agreement with themselves (SDA Conditions Rule, section 9(3)).

POL-SDA-01 Specialist Disability Accommodation Policy is the frame that points to this policy. POL-SDA-05 Tenancy Management Policy (Specialist Disability Accommodation) covers how we manage the tenancy after the agreement is signed.

3Commitments

C1

We will provide SDA to a participant only under a written agreement we developed with them, or a they hold a copy of. We use AGR-SDA-01 SDA Service Agreement.

Answers: Legislation (1). How we do it: Procedure step 1, Procedure step 11, Procedure step 15, Procedure step 17, Procedure step 18.

C2

We will develop each agreement with the participant, using their choices. Each one meets the SDA Conditions Rule, the SDA Rules 2020 and the that applies. The terms the requires are fixed terms in AGR-SDA-01. The checks the current addendum and the tenancy-law notice rules every 12 months and when either changes, and records the check in REG-SDA-02 col AU and col AV.

Answers: Legislation (1). How we do it: Procedure step 4, Procedure step 10, Procedure step 12, Procedure step 14.

C3

We will write into every agreement the , how and when it is paid, and how receipts are given. We never charge rent above the limit in the SDA Rules 2020 without telling the and sending a valuer's certificate.

Answers: Legislation (2), Legislation (2)(a). How we do it: Procedure step 5, Procedure step 6, Procedure step 12.

C4

We will write into every agreement the and how we look after it, any and what it covers, and every other charge. We charge nothing that is not written there.

Answers: Legislation (2), Legislation (2)(b), Legislation (2)(c). How we do it: Procedure step 7, Procedure step 29.

C5

We will give written notice before any rent or board increase. Each agreement states the minimum notice: the longer of 60 days and what the tenancy law requires.

Answers: Legislation (2), Legislation (2)(e). How we do it: Procedure step 7, Procedure step 23.

C6

We will name in every agreement our agent and the agent's responsibilities, or our own address and telephone number. We tell the participant in writing within 5 of any change to them. If the law sets a different period, we use that period.

Answers: Legislation (2), Legislation (2)(f), Legislation (2)(i), Legislation (2)(ii), Legislation (2)(g). How we do it: Procedure step 8, Procedure step 22.

C7

We will state in every agreement when it starts, how long it lasts and how it continues or is extended. We also state when the participant or we can end it. We end an agreement only for a reason written in it.

Answers: Legislation (2), Legislation (2)(h), Legislation (2)(j). How we do it: Procedure step 12, Procedure step 24, Procedure step 25.

C8

We will give a participant at least 90 days' written notice before they must leave their dwelling. We give shorter notice only to address a to them or to others. We do this only where the law allows it, and only when the Chief Executive has approved it in writing.

Answers: Legislation (2), Legislation (2)(k). How we do it: Procedure step 25, Procedure step 26, Procedure step 27, Procedure step 28.

C9

We will explain in every agreement how a participant asks for repairs and maintenance, and keep to the repair times we write in it. We keep every in a good state of repair.

Answers: Legislation (2), Legislation (2)(l). How we do it: Procedure step 8, Procedure step 12.

C10

We will set out in every agreement what each side can expect. This covers our responsibilities for the dwelling, and the participant's rights and responsibilities in using it. A participant's home never depends on who provides their supports.

Answers: Legislation (3). How we do it: Procedure step 12, Procedure step 14.

C11

We will include in every agreement the dwelling's safety features, including fire alarms, and how to get out of the building. We give the same information to each provider who delivers supported independent living in the dwelling.

Answers: Legislation (4). How we do it: Procedure step 9, Procedure step 20, Procedure step 21.

C12

We will support each participant to understand their agreement, in the language, mode of communication and terms they understand best. We give them time to decide, a supporter or advocate of their choice, and a record of what they said or showed back.

Answers: Legislation (5). How we do it: Procedure step 2, Procedure step 3, Procedure step 11, Procedure step 12, Procedure step 13.

C13

We will give each participant a copy signed by them and by us. When we cannot, we record the circumstances and offer the copy again until they have it.

Answers: Legislation (6). How we do it: Procedure step 17, Procedure step 18.

C14

We will record every agreement, change, review and ending in REG-SDA-02. We review each agreement with the participant at least every 12 months. We check our own work every 3 months.

Answers: Legislation (1), Legislation (6). How we do it: Procedure step 19, Procedure step 24.

C15

We will tell the participant within 5 business days when we learn that their SDA funding has changed or ended, or that their plan's design category has changed. We help them seek review, agree any rent change in writing with at least 60 days' notice, and do not end the agreement for that reason alone for at least 90 days.

4Ground rules

G1

Each participant has their own agreement for their own dwelling. We never use one agreement for a household.

G2

Housing and supports are separate agreements. Nothing in an SDA agreement makes a participant's home depend on using our supports or those of a provider we name.

G3

Where tenancy law gives a participant more than our agreement, the participant has what the law gives. The agreement never takes a legal right away. Where a state or territory Act allows notice shorter than 90 days, we still give 90 days unless the Chief Executive records a risk of harm.

G4

We never ask a participant to sign a blank or unfinished agreement, or to sign before they have had time to think.

G5

A signature is not proof of understanding. We record what the participant said or showed back, in their words.

G6

Nobody signs for an adult participant without legal authority that covers the agreement. PRO-SDA-04 Decision table 2 says who may sign.

G7

We never charge rent above the limit in SDA Rules 2020, section 29(1)(g), unless the Chief Executive agrees. The SDA Manager then tells the NDIA and sends a valuer's certificate.

G8

We never end an agreement for any of these reasons:

  • the participant changed support provider
  • the participant made a complaint
  • the participant asked for a repair or a change
  • the participant made a choice that carries risk, or took advice from an advocate
  • we want the dwelling for someone else.

PRO-SDA-04 Decision table 3 lists the reasons we may use.

G9

The Chief Executive approves every notice to end an agreement before it is given. A under PRO-SDA-03 Conflict of Interest Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation) comes first.

G10

An agent follows this policy and PRO-SDA-04. We stay responsible for what an agent does. The agent's responsibilities are written in the agreement.

G11

A sole trader holds every role. A sole trader names [independent contact for concerns] in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register. That person makes the second check of each draft (PRO-SDA-04 step 10), decides any rent above the limit (PRO-SDA-04 step 6), makes the tenure check (PRO-SDA-03 step 23), approves any notice shorter than 90 days (PRO-SDA-04 step 26) and any notice to end an agreement (PRO-SDA-05 step 24), and hears any concern about the sole trader.

G12

Every worker who works on agreements learns PRO-SDA-04 before they do so, and again every 12 months. REG-HRM-02 Training and Competency Register records it.

G13

We keep each agreement and every change for 7 years after it ends (NDIS Act 2013, section 45B, from 27 August 2026: records of claims and supports are kept for 7 years). The participant can have a copy at any time.

  • National Disability Insurance Scheme (Code of Conduct) Rules 2018, section 6(1)(a), (b) and (d).
  • Privacy Act 1988 (Cth).
  • The residential tenancy, building and fire safety law of [state or territory], and the guardianship law of [state or territory].

9Words we use

411 words
specialist disability accommodation (SDA)
a home for a person with extreme functional impairment or very high support needs. It does not include the supports the person gets while they live there.
enrolled dwelling
a dwelling the NDIA has enrolled so that SDA can be provided in it.
agreement
the completed AGR-SDA-01 for one participant and one dwelling, with every change to it.
proposed agreement
an agreement we worked out with the participant and gave them a copy of, before they have signed it.
tenancy law
the residential tenancy law of [state or territory] that applies to the dwelling.
rent
what the participant pays to live in the dwelling.
reasonable rent contribution
the part of the rent a participant is expected to pay, as the NDIS Pricing Arrangements for Specialist Disability Accommodation (current year) set it: currently 25 per cent of the basic Disability Support Pension plus 100 per cent of any Commonwealth Rent Assistance. The rent limit is the SDA amount in the participant's plan plus this contribution.
bond
money held as security against unpaid rent or damage. It may be nothing.
board
a payment, if the participant chooses it, for things we agree to provide, such as food or household costs.
agent
a person or business that acts for us on a dwelling, such as a property manager.
NDIA
the National Disability Insurance Agency.
NDIA addendum
the addendum to the NDIA's Terms of Business for Registered Providers that lists the terms an SDA agreement must include.
decision maker
a person with legal authority to decide for the participant, such as a guardian, a financial administrator, an attorney or a nominee.
risk of harm
a real and present chance that the participant or another person will be seriously hurt. We show it with facts, and never with a diagnosis or a label.
supported independent living (SIL) provider
a provider who gives a participant help with, or supervision of, daily tasks in their home.
tenure check
the Chief Executive's decision, before a notice goes out, on whether anything links it to the participant's support decisions or concerns.
business day
a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives.
SDA Rules 2020, SDA Conditions Rule
short names for the instruments in Authority.
SDA Manager
the Service Manager for our SDA dwellings.
Tenancy Officer
the worker the SDA Manager assigns tenancy tasks to. In a small provider this is the SDA Manager.

1Purpose

The result: every participant in one of our dwellings has a written they helped to shape and understood. They hold a signed copy of it. The money, the notice periods, the repairs and the safety information are written in it. Every change and every ending follows it.

This procedure gives effect to POL-SDA-03 Service Agreements with Participants Policy (Specialist Disability Accommodation), C1 to C15.

2When and who

Start this procedure at the step that matches what has happened:

  • A participant has accepted a place in one of our dwellings, or we find a participant living in one with no agreement: start at step 1.
  • A safety feature or the way out of the building changes: step 21.
  • Our , our address or our telephone number changes: step 22.
  • or is going up: step 23.
  • The agreement is due for review, the participant asks to see or change it, or a fixed term is near its end: step 24.
  • We think we may need to end an agreement: step 25. Steps 25 to 27 prepare the notice. PRO-SDA-05 Tenancy Management Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation) steps 24 to 27 serve it.
  • A participant gives us notice that they are leaving: PRO-SDA-05 step 28 ends the tenancy. Then do step 28 here.

Who acts:

  • The prepares the agreement, explains it, gives the copy and keeps the records.
  • The checks every draft, decides changes, signs for us, tells the and decides whether we may end an agreement.
  • The Chief Executive decides whether to charge rent above the limit and approves every notice to end an agreement.
  • The Quality Manager samples the records every 3 months.
  • Every worker tells the Tenancy Officer within 1 when a participant asks about, or wants to change, their agreement.

If an agent does the Tenancy Officer's work, the agent follows this procedure. [Provider name] stays responsible, and the SDA Manager checks the agent's work at step 10.

In a small provider one person may hold several of these roles. A sole trader holds them all. A sole trader still needs a second person for steps 6, 10, 25 (the at PRO-SDA-03 step 23) and 26, and for the approval of any notice to end an agreement at PRO-SDA-05 step 24. REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register names that person as [independent contact for concerns].

A business day is a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives. The SDA Manager is the Service Manager for our SDA dwellings. The Tenancy Officer is the worker the SDA Manager assigns tenancy tasks to; in a small provider this is the SDA Manager. The agreement is the completed AGR-SDA-01 SDA Service Agreement for one participant and one dwelling, with every change. A is an agreement we have worked out with the participant and given them a copy of, before they have signed it.

Short names used here:

  • SDA Rules 2020: the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation) Rules 2020
  • SDA Conditions Rule: the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation Conditions) Rule 2018
  • NDIA: the National Disability Insurance Agency
  • NDIS Commission: the NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission

3Before you start

  • You have the current AGR-SDA-01 SDA Service Agreement. Use the template itself. Do not start from an old signed copy.
  • You can open REG-SDA-02 SDA Tenancy and Vacancy Register, REG-SDA-01 SDA Dwelling Register and REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register.
  • You have the dwelling's latest FRM-SDA-03 SDA Dwelling Inspection and Compliance Checklist.
  • You have the participant's FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form, or you will complete one at step 2.
  • You have STA-SDA-01 SDA Service Agreement: Plain Summary in the participant's format.
  • You know how PRO-SDA-05 Tenancy Management Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation) and PRO-SDA-01 Enrolment of SDA Properties Procedure fit with this one. PRO-SDA-05 opens the tenancy row, serves notices and ends tenancies. PRO-SDA-01 deals with repairs.
  • You know these contacts: [repair contact], [urgent number], [advocacy service] and [tenancy advice service]. You know the NDIS Commission number, 1800 035 544.
  • You have done PRO-SDA-03 Conflict of Interest Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation) steps 5 to 8 with this participant, or you will do them before step 11.
  • REG-HRM-02 Training and Competency Register shows you have done the training for this procedure under PRO-HRM-03 Training and Competency Procedure.

Law changing: from 20 November 2026 the NDIS Act 2013 bans inducements to provide supports (new section 73VA, inserted by the NDIS Amendment (Securing the NDIS for Future Generations) Act 2026, Schedule 2 Part 8; the Department publishes 27 November 2026, so confirm the day). PRO-SDA-03 step 4 and step 11 of this procedure already bar any gift, discount or other benefit tied to a participant's choice.

4Watch out

  • Danger comes first. If anyone is in danger, call 000 before you do anything else on this page. A repair or a form can wait. A person in danger cannot.
  • No agreement, no stay. Providing SDA with no signed agreement, and no proposed agreement in the participant's hands, breaks a condition of registration (SDA Conditions Rule, section 9(1)). A civil penalty can follow (NDIS Act 2013, section 73J).
  • A signature is not understanding. A participant who signs without understanding can lose rights they did not know they had. Step 13 asks them to say or show it back.
  • A carer cannot sign for an adult. A family member or carer with no legal authority cannot sign for a participant. An agreement they sign may not hold, and the participant is left without one.
  • Rent above the limit. Charging rent above the limit without telling the NDIA breaks a condition of enrolment. The NDIA can cancel the dwelling's enrolment (SDA Rules 2020, section 27).
  • Fewer than 90 days. Shorter notice can leave a participant with nowhere to go. Only the Chief Executive can approve it, in writing, and only for a .
  • A notice after a support choice. A notice soon after a participant changes support provider looks like punishment. Step 25 needs the tenure check first.
  • Missing safety information. A provider who does not know the exits and the alarms may not get the participant out in a fire. PRO-SDA-05 step 14 gives it to a new provider before their first shift. Step 21 sends any change.
  • The 5 business days to tell the NDIA. The time is set by law. PRO-SDA-05 step 2 tells the NDIA. Missing the time breaks a condition of enrolment.

5Steps

Get ready (the Tenancy Officer)

Step 1

The Tenancy Officer

Open an agreement record for the participant and the dwelling.

Open it when the participant accepts a place, or when you find a participant living in a dwelling with no agreement. Copy the dwelling details from its row in REG-SDA-01. Check the number of residents it is enrolled for. Check the participant's plan includes SDA funding, and write the date you saw it. Complete the first questions of AGR-SDA-01.

Result
One agreement record exists for this participant and this dwelling.
Record
AGR-SDA-01 Q1 to Q2; REG-SDA-02
Time limit
Within 2 business days of the participant accepting the place (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C1.

Step 2

The Tenancy Officer

Ask the participant how they want to take part.

Ask which language, way of communicating and format they want, and who they want with them. Copy the answers from FRM-RGT-01. If it is more than 12 months old, ask again. Book an interpreter, a communication partner, a supporter or an advocate if they want one. Offer to meet at the dwelling or where they choose.

Result
Every meeting about the agreement will be in the way the participant understands best.
Record
AGR-SDA-01 Q28
Time limit
Before the participant sees any draft (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C12.

Step 3

Warning. A family member or carer with no legal authority cannot sign for an adult. An agreement they sign may not bind the participant.

The Tenancy Officer

Confirm who decides about this agreement.

Start from the participant deciding, with support if they want it. Ask whether anyone has legal authority to decide for them, such as a guardian, a financial administrator, an attorney or a nominee. Ask to see the document. Check it covers a housing or tenancy agreement. Write what it covers, the date you saw it and where the copy is filed. Decision table 2 says who may sign. Involve the participant whoever signs.

Result
You know who signs, and on what authority.
Record
AGR-SDA-01 Q3
Time limit
Before the draft is prepared (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C12.

Step 4

The Tenancy Officer

Check the law that applies to this agreement.

Copy the current notice rule rows for [state or territory] from REG-SDA-02 col AU (entry, rent change, breach, ending by us, ending by the participant) and the date each was checked at col AV. Copy the date the SDA Manager last checked the . Ask the SDA Manager if any row or check is older than 12 months, or if you are unsure. From those rows, write each rule that gives the participant a longer period, a lower limit or an extra step. Write whether the applies to this dwelling and, if it does, the prescribed agreement form and how this agreement sits with it, as the tenancy-law review for [state or territory] decided. The terms the NDIA addendum requires are fixed terms in AGR-SDA-01; write only the addendum version checked at Q6.

Result
The draft will meet the tenancy law and the terms the NDIA requires.
Record
AGR-SDA-01 Q4 to Q6
Time limit
On the day you prepare the draft (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C2.

Prepare the draft

Step 5

Warning. Charging rent above the limit without telling the NDIA breaks a condition of enrolment.

The SDA Manager

Set the rent and check it against the limit.

Work out the rent from the income support and rent assistance figures the participant gave you. The limit is the SDA amount in the participant's plan plus the as the NDIS Pricing Arrangements for Specialist Disability Accommodation (current year) set it (currently 25 per cent of the basic Disability Support Pension plus 100 per cent of any Commonwealth Rent Assistance). Compare the total rent we propose to charge with that limit. Write the figures and how the rent was worked out, in plain words. If the total is above the limit, do step 6 before the draft goes to the participant.

Result
The rent is within the limit, or step 6 is under way.
Record
AGR-SDA-01 Q7 to Q8
Time limit
Before the draft is prepared (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C3.

Step 6

The Chief Executive

If the rent we propose is above the limit:

Decide whether to charge rent above the limit.

Charge it only if a qualified property valuer certifies that the rent is fair and reasonable. If you agree, the SDA Manager tells the NDIA and attaches the certificate, at PRO-SDA-05 step 2. Tell the participant what you decided, in their way of communicating. If you do not agree, lower the rent to the limit and go back to step 5. A sole trader asks [independent contact for concerns].

Result
The rent is within the limit, or the NDIA has been told and the participant knows.
Record
AGR-SDA-01 Q8
Time limit
Before the draft is checked at step 10. The NDIA is told within 5 business days of proposing the rent (statutory: SDA Rules 2020, section 29(2))

Carries out: Policy C3.

Step 7

The Tenancy Officer

Complete the , board, other charges and the notice before an increase.

Write the bond, which may be nothing, and where it is held. Never ask for more than the tenancy law of [state or territory] allows. Write board only if the participant chose it. Write every other charge, or "none". Write the days of notice before rent or board goes up: the longer of 60 days and what the tenancy law of [state or territory] requires. Nothing is charged that is not written here.

Result
Every amount the participant will pay is written, and nothing else will be charged.
Record
AGR-SDA-01 Q11 to Q15
Time limit
Before the draft is checked at step 10 (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C4, Policy C5.

Step 8

The Tenancy Officer

Complete who the participant deals with, and how to ask for repairs.

If we use an agent, write the agent's name, telephone number, address and responsibilities. If not, write "no agent". Always write our address and telephone number. Write our repair contact and our urgent number. Ask the participant how they like to ask for repairs, and write it.

Result
The participant knows who to contact, and about what.
Record
AGR-SDA-01 Q16 to Q17 and Q24
Time limit
Before the draft is checked at step 10 (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C6, Policy C9.

Step 9

The Tenancy Officer

Complete the safety features, and the list of providers who need the safety information.

Copy the safety features from the dwelling's latest FRM-SDA-03. If an item is missing or not working, tell the SDA Manager the same day, and do not write it as working. Write the route and the meeting point for leaving the building. Ask the participant which providers deliver supported independent living in the dwelling, and write each one. PRO-SDA-05 step 14 gives each provider the information before their first shift. The agreement says so.

Result
The safety information is complete, true and ready to explain.
Record
AGR-SDA-01 Q25 and Q27
Time limit
Before the draft is checked at step 10 (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C11.

Step 10

The SDA Manager

Check the draft.

A person who did not prepare it checks it. Check every question has an answer. Check the terms are the current AGR-SDA-01, and that nothing protecting the participant has been cut. That includes 90 days' notice, the repair times and the grounds for ending. Check the rent against its limit, the law against Q4 to Q6, and the safety features against the latest inspection. Check PRO-SDA-03 steps 7 and 8 are on track to reach the participant at least 3 business days before they are asked to sign. A sole trader asks [independent contact for concerns].

Result
The draft is complete and correct before the participant sees it.
Record
AGR-SDA-01 Q38
Time limit
Within 3 business days of the draft being complete (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C2.

Explain and agree (the Tenancy Officer)

Step 11

The Tenancy Officer

Give the participant the draft and the plain summary, with time to think.

Give them AGR-SDA-01 and STA-SDA-01 in their format. Add our conflict of interest policy and statement of interests. Add the tenancy information from [state or territory], how to complain, how to find an advocate and the house rules, if there are any. Tell them they can take it away, show a person they trust, and ask for changes. Offer at least 5 business days to think. They can sign sooner if they choose to. Offer no gift, discount or reward for signing.

Result
The participant has everything, in their format, and time to decide.
Record
AGR-SDA-01 Q29 and Q31
Time limit
At least 5 business days before the participant is asked to sign, unless they choose to sign sooner (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C1, Policy C12.

Step 12

The Tenancy Officer

Go through the agreement with the participant, one topic at a time.

Use the language, mode and format from step 2. Cover eight topics in this order. First, your home and your supports. Then rent and other money, who you deal with, dates and ending, repairs, safety and the way out, your rights, and your responsibilities. Ask the participant to choose how they pay rent and get receipts. Agree the start date, how long it lasts, the review date and the notice each side gives. PRO-SDA-02 Rights and Responsibilities Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation) steps 2 and 3 can happen at the same meeting. Stop when the participant is tired and carry on another day. Write who was there and how you explained it.

Result
The participant has heard each topic in a way they can follow, and has made their own choices.
Record
AGR-SDA-01 Q9 to Q10, Q18 to Q23, Q26 and Q30
Time limit
Within 10 business days of step 11, or later if the participant asks (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C2, Policy C3, Policy C7, Policy C9, Policy C10, Policy C12.

Step 13

Warning. A signature does not show that someone understood. A participant who signs without understanding can lose rights they did not know they had.

The Tenancy Officer

Ask the participant to say or show back what the main terms mean.

Ask five things. What will you pay, and when? How much notice would you get if we asked you to leave? How do you ask for a repair? What do you do if there is a fire? Who can help you if you are unhappy? Write what they said or showed, in their words. If they cannot answer, explain it another way and try again at another meeting. This is not a test. Write anything still to explain, with a date.

Result
You know what the participant understands, and what is still to explain.
Record
AGR-SDA-01 Q32
Time limit
At the end of the last meeting, and before step 15 (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C12.

Step 14

The SDA Manager

Decide each change the participant asks for.

Agree to a change that is better for the participant, or neutral, unless the law stops it. Do not agree to a term that is worse for the participant than the standard terms, unless the law requires it. The standard terms include 90 days' notice, the grounds for ending, the repair times and rent within the limit. Tell the participant the answer and the reason in their way of communicating. Make each agreed change as a new version of the draft. If you cannot agree, offer another way and an advocate.

Result
Every change asked for has an answer and a reason.
Record
AGR-SDA-01 Q33
Time limit
Within 5 business days of the change being asked (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C2, Policy C10.

Sign and give the copy

Step 15

Warning. A participant who signs under pressure may not have understood or agreed. The agreement may not stand, and the participant may lose trust in us.

The Tenancy Officer

Ask the participant to sign.

Check Q3 and Decision table 2 for who signs. Check every question is answered and nothing is blank. Check PRO-SDA-03 step 7 and step 8 were done at least 3 business days ago, unless the participant asked for less in their own words. Let the participant sign in their own way, such as a signature, a mark or an electronic signature. Tell them they can wait. A supporter or advocate may sit with them but does not sign for them. If they do not want to sign yet, write why in their words and go to step 18.

Result
The participant signs by choice, or chooses to wait.
Record
AGR-SDA-01 Q34
Time limit
After step 13, and at least 5 business days after step 11 unless the participant chooses sooner (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C1.

Step 16

The SDA Manager

Sign for [Provider name].

Sign as the person named in REG-GOV-01. An agent signs only if the agent holds that authority in writing.

Result
The agreement is signed by both of us.
Record
AGR-SDA-01 Q35
Time limit
Within 1 business day of the participant signing (our standard)
Step 17

The Tenancy Officer

Give the participant a copy signed by both of us.

Give it in the participant's format, with the plain summary. Use paper, large print, email, a read-aloud recording or pictures, as they choose. If the participant would rather not keep a copy at home, keep it safe for them and give it whenever they ask. If you cannot give the copy, write the circumstances on the same day. Offer it again within 5 business days and at each review until they have it.

Result
The participant has their copy, or the reason they do not is written down.
Record
AGR-SDA-01 Q37
Time limit
Within 2 business days of the last signature (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C1, Policy C13.

Step 18

The SDA Manager

If the participant has not signed:

Provide the dwelling under the proposed agreement.

Check the participant holds a copy of the proposed agreement. Check we worked it out with them at steps 11 to 14. Check we will provide the dwelling exactly as it says. This is the second way SDA may lawfully be provided (SDA Conditions Rule, section 9(1)(b)). Write the participant's reason in their words, the date SDA began and the date you will talk with them again. Talk with them again within 10 business days. Not signing is not a reason to end the agreement or to take their home.

Result
The participant has a copy and their home does not wait for a signature.
Record
AGR-SDA-01 Q36
Time limit
Before we provide the dwelling (statutory: SDA Conditions Rule, section 9(1))

Carries out: Policy C1, Policy C13.

Step 19

The Tenancy Officer

Make sure the agreement is in the participant's tenancy row in REG-SDA-02.

For a new participant, the SDA Manager opens the tenancy row at PRO-SDA-05 step 11, from the signed agreement. Give the SDA Manager the agreement. Check the row shows the agreement date, the route, the copy, the rent, the rent limit check and the bond. For a participant already living in the dwelling, open the tenancy row yourself and fill columns Q to U from the agreement. Write the row reference.

Result
The agreement can be found and checked from the register.
Record
AGR-SDA-01 Q39; REG-SDA-02 col Q; REG-SDA-02 col R
Time limit
Within 2 business days of both of us signing, or of step 18 (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C14.

After the participant moves in

Step 20

Warning. A participant who has not practised leaving may not get out in a fire. A smoke alarm that is covered or disabled may not warn them.

The Tenancy Officer

Practise leaving the building with the participant.

Walk the route to the meeting point with them, in their way of communicating. Show them each smoke alarm. Tell them never to cover or disable one. Use what they need to get out, such as a flashing alarm, equipment or help from a person. Where the participant needs help from a person to get out, the SIL provider's worker is present and takes part, and the practice date is also recorded at AGR-SDA-02 Q13. With their consent, link it to their FRM-SUP-07 Participant Emergency and Disaster Plan. Write what happened. Tell the SDA Manager the same day about anything that does not work.

Result
The participant has practised getting out, and anything that does not work is being fixed.
Record
AGR-SDA-01 Q26
Time limit
Within 5 business days of the participant moving in, and after any change to the safety features (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C11.

Step 21

The Tenancy Officer

If a safety feature or the way out of the building changes:

Send the changed safety information to the participant and to each provider.

A change can come from an inspection on FRM-SDA-03, a repair or a new feature. Change Q25 and Q26 as a new version of the agreement, as in step 24. Give the participant the changed copy and explain it. Send the changed features and way out, in writing, to each provider who delivers supported independent living in the dwelling. Send information about the participant's own needs only with consent on FRM-INF-01 Consent to Collect, Use and Share Information Form. Write who, when and how. A new provider gets it from PRO-SDA-05 step 14.

Result
The participant and every provider know the changed safety features and the way out.
Record
AGR-SDA-01 Q27; REG-SDA-02 col AB
Time limit
Within 5 business days of the change (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C11.

During the agreement

Step 22

The Tenancy Officer

Tell the participant in writing about a change to our agent or our details.

This covers our address, our telephone number, the agent's name, address and telephone number, and the agent's responsibilities. Write to the participant in their format. If the tenancy law of [state or territory] sets a different period, use it. Change the answer as a new version and give the participant the changed copy.

Result
The participant knows who to contact and where.
Record
AGR-SDA-01 Q41
Time limit
Within 5 business days of the change (our standard, from Quality Indicators Guidelines section 70 (2)(g))

Carries out: Policy C6.

Step 23

The SDA Manager

Set the notice for a rent or board increase.

Check the new rent against the limit, as in step 5. If it is above the limit, do step 6 first. Write the new amount, the date it starts and why. Give the participant at least the days written in the agreement. Give more if the notice rule row in REG-SDA-02 says so. The Tenancy Officer gives the notice under PRO-SDA-05 steps 24, 26 and 27. If the limit on the rent goes down, lower the rent from the day it goes down.

Result
The notice period is right before the notice goes out.
Record
AGR-SDA-01 Q42; REG-SDA-02 col S
Time limit
The longer of what the tenancy law of [state or territory] requires and 60 days before the increase starts (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C5.

Step 24

The Tenancy Officer

Review the agreement with the participant.

Review it at least every 12 months, when the participant asks, and when something important changes. Ask what is working and what is not. Go through the main terms again, as in steps 12 and 13. Change the agreement only with the participant's agreement, except a change the law requires or a notice under step 22 or step 23. Save each change as a new dated version and keep the old one. Give the participant the changed copy, as in step 17. For a fixed term, write at least 90 days before the end date to confirm that it continues on the same terms.

Result
The agreement is current, and the participant has the changed copy.
Record
AGR-SDA-01 Q40, Q43 and Q44
Time limit
Every 12 months. A changed copy within 2 business days of the change. A fixed term letter at least 90 days before the end date (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C7, Policy C14.

Ending the agreement

Step 25

Warning. Ending an agreement can leave a person without a home. A reason we cannot use, or a missed step, can break the law and leave the participant homeless.

The SDA Manager

Check that the agreement lets us end it, and set the days of notice.

Use Decision table 3. Check the reason is on the list in the agreement, and is not one the agreement says we never use. Check the steps that must come first are done, and write what we tried, with dates. Send a tenure check request to the Chief Executive under PRO-SDA-03 steps 22 and 23, and wait for the decision. Set the notice at the days in Q23. That is at least 90, and longer where the law says. Offer the participant an independent advocate. Then go on at PRO-SDA-05 step 24, which checks the notice rule and gets the Chief Executive's approval. The participant's own notice does not need this step.

Result
Only a reason we may use goes forward, with the steps done and the days of notice set.
Record
AGR-SDA-01 Q45
Time limit
Before any notice is written (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C7, Policy C8.

Step 26

The Chief Executive

If we propose fewer than 90 days of notice:

Decide in writing whether shorter notice is needed.

Allow fewer days only where a risk of harm to the participant or to others needs it, and only where tenancy law allows it. Write the risk, and why 90 days would not keep people safe. Write your name and the date. The notice is never shorter than the law allows. When the notice is served, the Tenancy Officer tells the participant the reason in their way of communicating. A sole trader asks [independent contact for concerns].

Result
A shorter notice has a written reason before it is given.
Record
AGR-SDA-01 Q46; REG-SDA-02 col AX
Time limit
Before the notice is given (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C8.

Step 27

The SDA Manager

Check the days of notice before the notice is served.

Count the days from the date the law treats the notice as received to the date the participant must leave. The count must be at least the days in Q23, or the days step 26 approved. Write the dates and the days. If the count is short, change the date to leave. Then the Tenancy Officer serves the notice under PRO-SDA-05 steps 24 to 27, and tells the participant how to seek a review. PRO-SDA-05 step 2 tells the NDIA within 5 business days.

Result
The notice gives the days the agreement promises.
Record
AGR-SDA-01 Q46; REG-SDA-02 col AZ
Time limit
Before the notice is served (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C8.

Step 28

The Tenancy Officer

Settle the bond and give the participant a final statement.

PRO-SDA-05 step 28 ends the tenancy and does the final inspection. This step applies the agreement's own terms. Give a final rent statement. Return the bond within the days in Q12. Keep back only unpaid rent, or damage the participant caused beyond fair wear and tear. Before you ask for any damage payment, check whether a missing support or adjustment caused it. Show the evidence in writing first and say how to dispute it. Write the keys returned.

Result
The participant has their bond, or the evidence for what was kept, and a final statement.
Record
AGR-SDA-01 Q47; REG-SDA-02 col U
Time limit
Within the days written in the agreement, and never later than tenancy law allows (our standard, and statutory: tenancy law of [state or territory])

Carries out: Policy C8.

Step 29

The SDA Manager

Close the agreement.

Check that Q45 to Q47 are complete, and that REG-SDA-02 col W shows how the tenancy ended. Check the participant was helped to find a home, with the supporters they chose. Write anything we learned in REG-QMS-01 Continuous Improvement Register. File the agreement and every change. Keep them for 7 years after it ends (NDIS Act 2013, section 45B, from 27 August 2026).

Result
The agreement is closed, with every record in place.
Record
AGR-SDA-01 Q47; REG-SDA-02 col W
Time limit
Within 10 business days of the participant leaving (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C4.

The participant's needs are beyond what the dwelling can meetThe request handled under PRO-SDA-02 steps 15 to 28. Advice from the participant's practitioners. The participant chooses what happens next. Their other supports are not touched
No contact for [set at adoption] days: the period the tenancy law of [state or territory] sets for abandoned premises, where it sets oneCalls, messages and a letter. Contact with their emergency contact and support coordinator. A welfare check under PRO-INC-01 Incident Management Procedure, and a police welfare check where there is any concern for their safety. The abandonment process of the tenancy law, from the REG-SDA-02 notice rule rows
A change or choice of support provider, including a SIL provider, a complaint, a request for a repair or a change, a choice that carries risk, advice from an advocate, a refusal to sign an arrangement or this agreement, or someone else wanting the homeNot a reason. The agreement continues

7If it goes wrong

IfThen
A participant asks a worker about their agreementDo not guess. Tell the Tenancy Officer within 1 business day. Give the participant the repair contact from AGR-SDA-01 Q24 if they need a repair
A participant has an urgent repair, or anyone is in dangerCall 000 if anyone is in danger. Otherwise phone the urgent number in AGR-SDA-01 Q24 and tell the SDA Manager. Make it safe within 24 hours, and the same day where a resident's safety or a life-support device depends on it. Follow PRO-INC-01 if anyone was hurt
The participant does not want the agreement, or a termWrite it in their words at Q33 or Q36. Ask what they want changed. Offer an advocate and more time. The SDA Manager decides at step 14. A term the law gives them stays. Their home does not wait for a signature (step 18)
The participant decides not to take the placeRespect it. Write their words. Close the agreement record and tell the SDA Manager. Offer help to look at other options, with their support coordinator if they agree. Hand the vacancy to PRO-SDA-05 step 1. It counts for nothing against them
The participant says after signing that they did not understandStop. Explain again, as in steps 12 and 13. Record it at Q40. The SDA Manager decides whether the agreement is made again. Nothing is held against the participant
An interpreter or communication partner is not availableDo not go on without one. Rebook within 5 business days. Use a family member only if the participant chooses it
The law, the NDIA addendum or the template changed since the draftDo step 4 again. Tell the participant what changed. Save a new version. Do not ask them to sign the old one
The plan, the participant's income or the SDA amount has changedDo step 5 again. Tell the participant before the new rent applies
A time limit in this procedure will be missedTell the participant before it passes. Give the reason and the new date, and write both beside the question. A time the law sets cannot be moved
The 5 business days to tell the NDIA cannot be met, or the NDIA cannot be reachedTell the Chief Executive the same day. Keep trying and write each time. Tell the NDIA in writing as soon as you can reach it, at PRO-SDA-05 step 2, and record the reason in REG-QMS-01. Never leave it undone
We find a participant living in a dwelling with no agreementTell the SDA Manager the same day. Start at step 1 and give them a proposed agreement within 2 business days. The Chief Executive records the gap in REG-QMS-01, decides whether to notify the NDIS Commission using PRO-GOV-02 Notification of Changes and Events Procedure, and records the reason for any decision not to notify
The Tenancy Officer is awayThe SDA Manager acts. If both are away, the Chief Executive names someone the same day. No step is skipped
The agent does not follow this procedureThe SDA Manager takes the step over the same day. Write it in REG-QMS-01. The agent's responsibilities in AGR-SDA-01 Q16 are reviewed
A family member or another person pressures the participant to sign, or not to signDo not accept it. Talk with the participant alone, if they agree. Tell the SDA Manager the same day. If the participant is at risk, follow PRO-SGD-01
A participant disputes the rent, the bond or a chargeAcknowledge it within 1 business day. Treat it as a complaint under POL-FBK-01 Feedback and Complaints Management Policy. Tell them they can go to the tribunal or other body of [state or territory]. Make no tenancy action while it is open
A colleague, agent or manager pressures a participant, links their home to their supports, or forges or backdates a signatureTell the Chief Executive. If it is about the Chief Executive, tell [independent contact for concerns]. You can phone the NDIS Commission on 1800 035 544. POL-GOV-03 Whistleblower and Disclosure Protection Policy protects you
The participant gives notice by phone or in personAccept it. Write it down with them, in their words, and confirm it in writing. Go to PRO-SDA-05 step 28, then step 28 here
The system is downUse a paper AGR-SDA-01. The Tenancy Officer enters it within 1 business day of the system coming back

8Done means

The agreement is in place when all of these are true:

  • the participant has a copy signed by both of us
  • if they do not, the circumstances are written down and a date is set to offer the copy again
  • if the participant has not signed, they hold the proposed agreement and we provide their home under its terms
  • every question in Sections A to I of AGR-SDA-01 has an answer
  • the safety information is with every provider who delivers supported independent living in the dwelling
  • the agreement is entered in REG-SDA-02.

These records now exist:

  • the completed AGR-SDA-01 in the participant's file, with its dated versions
  • the record of how the agreement was explained, in REG-RGT-01 Communication and Accessible Information Register
  • the entry in REG-SDA-02, with the row reference at Q39
  • any rent-limit notice to the NDIA, and the valuer's certificate
  • for an ending: the days of notice at Q46, the Chief Executive's written decision for any notice under 90 days, the bond and final statement at Q47, and the closing entry in REG-SDA-02.

9Quick card

146 words
  • Do not provide the dwelling until the participant holds a signed or proposed agreement (step 18)
  • Ask who decides, and see the legal document before anyone signs for an adult (step 3)
  • Check the rent against the limit before you offer it (step 5)
  • Ask the participant to say or show back what the terms mean (step 13)
  • Give a signed copy within 2 business days, or write down why not (step 17)
  • Send changed safety information to every provider within 5 business days (step 21)
  • Tell the participant in writing within 5 business days if our agent or our details change (step 22)
  • Send the tenure check to the Chief Executive before any notice to end an agreement (step 25)
  • Never end an agreement without the Chief Executive's written approval, and at least 90 days' notice unless there is a risk of harm (step 26)

register.proves:
This register is the one running record of how [Provider name] looks after each dwelling. It shows how we enrol it, keep it inside its enrolment, and keep it safe, secure, private and in good repair. Each row is one record about one dwelling. A row shows what was found or decided, who did it, which residents were told, and when the next action falls due.

  • Indicators evidenced: s 71 (1), s 71 (2) and s 71 (3).
  • The modification columns also evidence s 68 (1) and s 72 (5). FRM-SDA-01 Dwelling Modification and Adjustment Request sends its rows here.
  • Legal basis: Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 7, clause 6. SDA Conditions Rule, sections 6, 8, 9, 10 and 11. SDA Rules 2020, sections 5 to 8, 15, 19 and 24 to 32.
  • The SDA Rules 2020 are the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation) Rules 2020. The SDA Conditions Rule is the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation Conditions) Rule 2018.
  • No law sets the columns of this register. They are our standard, built from what the law makes us certify, notify and keep.
  • Retention: keep each row for 7 years from the day it is closed or superseded. Keep a dwelling row for 7 years after the dwelling stops being enrolled with us (our standard). NDIS Act 2013, section 45B (from 27 August 2026): records of claims and supports are kept for 7 years; this register's rows support SDA claims, so 7 years is also the statutory floor.
  • Other law can require a certificate or a safety record to be kept longer. Check the law of [state or territory] before any row is destroyed.
  • Roles and words: : the Service Manager for our SDA dwellings. : the worker the SDA Manager assigns tenancy tasks to; in a small provider this is the SDA Manager. : a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives. List of laws: the dated list of state and territory laws kept once in REG-QMS-03 Compliance Obligations Register.

The register holds ten types of row. Column C names the type. Columns A to Q are the spine, and every row uses them. Each type then fills its own group of columns:

  • dwelling: columns R to AE
  • limits check: columns AF to AH
  • certificate or service: columns AI to AK
  • inspection: columns AL to AT
  • repair: columns AU to BA
  • modification record: columns BB to BG and BP to BT
  • entry record: column BH
  • matter: columns BI to BK
  • compliance check: columns BL to BM
  • house rules check: columns BN to BO

Residents' names are not kept here. A row uses resident numbers. A resident number is the number we use in place of a name, for example the participant's record number in REG-SUP-01 Participant and Service Register. Health details, behaviour support content and a resident's own words stay on their own file.

Keep each row type on its own sheet, with the spine columns first. A provider with one dwelling has few rows: one dwelling row, two inspections a year, and a handful of certificate or service rows.
register.entry:
1. The SDA Manager adds every row. The Tenancy Officer adds entry records and modification records, and may add a repair row from a resident's report. The Quality Manager adds compliance check rows, and inspection rows for a sample re-inspection. The person who enters a home records the entry the same day, and the Tenancy Officer adds the entry record. When the SDA Manager is away, the Tenancy Officer adds rows.
  2. Add the row within 2 business days of the event (our standard). Add an NDIA matter row, a repair row and its rating within 1 business day, and an emergency or urgent repair row the same day.
  3. Use one row for each limits check, certificate or service due, inspection, defect, modification request, entry and NDIA matter. An inspection that finds 3 defects makes 4 rows, plus a limits check row. Link them at col P.
  4. A dwelling has one dwelling row in force at a time. When a dwelling fact changes, add a new version of the row with the date, your name and the reason. The old version becomes "superseded".
  5. Never overwrite or delete an entry. A correction is a new version of the row, with the date, your name and the reason.
  6. Write resident numbers, not names. Leave out health details, behaviour support content and a resident's private words.
  7. Use one row each time a certificate or a service falls due. When it is done, close the row and open the next one.
  8. When someone was hurt or nearly hurt, the event is also an incident. Write its number from REG-INC-01 Incident Register at col P. A complaint goes in REG-FBK-01 Complaints Register. A hazard to people while supports are given goes in REG-ENV-01 Hazard and Maintenance Register. Tenancy facts go in REG-SDA-02 SDA Tenancy and Vacancy Register. Link each one here.
  9. At any time, each must show a dwelling row with the status "enrolled". It must show an inspection row and a limits check row, each not older than 6 months. Its certificate or service rows must not be past their due dates, and no repair row may be past its due date.
  10. Reopen a closed row when the defect comes back. Set col N to "reopened" and write the reason.

Which columns each row type fills:

Row typeUse it forColumns to fill
DwellingEach dwelling we enrol or plan to enrol. One row is in force at a timeA to L, N to AE
Limits checkEach check of numbers and density: before we apply, before a move-in, and at an inspectionA to H, K to Q, AF to AH
Certificate or serviceEach certificate, approval, service or test that falls dueA to H, K to Q, AI to AK
InspectionEach inspection, with the residentsA to Q, AL to AT
RepairEach defect, from report to closingA to Q, AU to BA
Modification recordEach change a participant asks for, sent here from FRM-SDA-01A to Q, BB to BG, BP to BT
Entry recordEach entry into a resident's home by us or a contractorA to I, M to Q, BH
NDIA matterEach notice we send the NDIA, and each notice, request or decision we receive from itA to H, J to Q, BI to BK
Compliance checkEach 12-monthly check of the list of laws, each check when the law changes, and the briefing of people who work at our dwellingsA to H, K to Q, BL and BM
House rules checkEach check of house rules, notices, forms and agreements against residents' rights, made under PRO-SDA-02A to Q, BN and BO

A row is closed only when all of these are true for its type:

  • Dwelling: a new version has replaced it, or the dwelling is no longer enrolled with us and the NDIA has been told.
  • Limits check: the result is recorded. If it was "over a limit", the Chief Executive has decided what happens.
  • Certificate or service: the certificate or report is filed, and the next one has its own row.
  • Inspection: every defect has its own row, each resident has been told the result, and the next inspection date is set.
  • Repair: the work is done, someone other than the contractor has checked it, the resident says it is fixed, and the resident has been told. Any NDIA matter row for it is also closed.
  • Modification record: FRM-SDA-01 question 37 is answered.
  • Entry record: the visit is recorded, with the time out and any key used.
  • NDIA matter: the notice or answer was sent, proof is filed, and the NDIA's reply is recorded. A notice we sent may close on "no reply" after 20 business days (our standard). An application for enrolment, a request from the NDIA and a notice from the NDIA stay open until the NDIA decides.
  • Compliance check: every change found has an owner and a due date.
  • House rules check: every limit found is removed, or has its lawful authority and the Chief Executive's decision on file. Each resident affected has been told.

The SDA Manager approves closing. The Quality Manager approves closing for an urgent repair row, an NDIA matter row and a dwelling row.

register.see:
• The SDA Manager, the Tenancy Officer, the Quality Manager and the Chief Executive can see every row.
  • A worker can see the open defects, entry records and certificate rows for each dwelling where they work. They need these to work safely.
  • A resident can ask to see every row about their dwelling and about them, and can ask us to correct it. A resident sees other residents' rows only with names and details removed.
  • A dwelling's owner can see repair rows and certificate or service rows for their dwelling, limited to the owner view: columns A to H, K to O, AU (the defect category only), AV, AX to AZ, and the certificate or service columns AI to AK. They see no resident's details, nothing at col I or col J, and no resident number.
  • A contractor sees only the repair row for their job.
  • The NDIA, the NDIS Commission, an auditor or a regulator sees rows only as the law allows or requires.

Rows about a person's home hold sensitive personal information. Keep the register in [system name], with a login for each person and a log of changes. Lock away any paper form or key log.

Photos show the defect, never a person. Take a photo in a resident's home only with their consent. Nobody keeps photos on a personal phone. POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy sets the wider privacy rules.
register.rows: The rows are the data. They are kept in the workbook or system built to this specification, not in this document. A workbook (.xlsx) generated from this column guide is supplied with the 0.3.0 set, with a Register sheet of the column headers and a Column guide sheet; at adoption it is completed with one sheet per row type, the spine columns first, drop-down lists for the allowed values, the calculated days at col BT, and entry rule 9 as its dashboard. Where a cell would otherwise hold a list (for example col I, col J, col AD, col AL or col BM), a second sheet holds one row per resident, matter, feature or event, linked by the record number at col A.

register.proves:
This register is the one running record of how [Provider name] manages each tenancy in its dwellings. Each row is one record. It shows what was done, who took part, what the participant said and chose, and who checked.

It holds nine kinds of record: tenancy, arrangement, vacancy, notice rule, notice, change, home event, concern and review. An arrangement is the with the participant's . A concern is anything raised about a dwelling that is not yet a complaint, a repair or an incident.

Complaints, incidents and repairs are not copied here. They stay in REG-FBK-01 Complaints Register, REG-INC-01 Incident Register and REG-SDA-01 SDA Dwelling Register. A row here links to them in column O.

In this register:

  • "SDA Conditions Rule" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation Conditions) Rule 2018.
  • "SDA Rules 2020" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation) Rules 2020.
  • "Incident Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Incident Management and Reportable Incidents) Rules 2018.
  • "Complaints Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Complaints Management and Resolution) Rules 2018.
  • "Restrictive Practices Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Restrictive Practices and Behaviour Support) Rules 2018.
  • "" means the Service Manager for our SDA dwellings. "" means the worker the SDA Manager assigns tenancy tasks to; in a small provider this is the SDA Manager. "" means a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives.
  • Indicators evidenced: s 72 (1) to (5), (8) and (9), including s 72 (3)(a) to (3)(h). Columns O and BL link to the complaints and incident records that evidence s 72 (6) and (7); those indicators are proved by the complaints and incident systems, not here. A SIL provider that signs an arrangement can use its arrangement row for Module 5A, sections 72A to 72E (from 1 July 2026).
  • Legal basis: NDIS Act 2013, section 73F(2)(a) and (c). It makes compliance with the law and the NDIS Practice Standards a condition of registration. The SDA Conditions Rule (sections 6 and 8 to 11) and the SDA Rules 2020 (sections 24, 29 and 32) set duties; section 37 of the SDA Rules 2020 is the equivalent of Conditions Rule section 10(2)(b) for registered providers of supports. This register evidences them. No NDIS rule sets the columns. They are our standard, built from the indicators and those duties.
  • Retention: keep each row for 7 years from the day it is closed or superseded (our standard). NDIS Act 2013, section 45B (from 27 August 2026): records of claims and supports are kept for 7 years, so 7 years is also the statutory floor. An incident or complaint record has its own limit. It is 7 years from the day it is made (statutory: Incident Rules, section 12(4); Complaints Rules, section 10(3)).
  • Other law can require longer, for example about . Check the law of [state or territory] before any row is destroyed.

Which columns apply:

  • Every row fills columns A to O. These are the spine.
  • A tenancy row also fills columns P to W.
  • An arrangement row also fills columns X to AH. Every tenancy has an arrangement row. Where no SIL provider delivers supports in the dwelling to the participant, the row says so and sets a date to check again.
  • A vacancy row also fills columns AI to AT.
  • A notice rule row fills columns AU and AV.
  • A notice row also fills columns AW to BE.
  • A change row also fills columns BF to BH.
  • A home event row also fills columns BI to BN.
  • A review row also fills column BO.
  • A concern row also fills columns BP to BS.
register.entry:
1. The SDA Manager owns the register and approves the closing of every row. The Tenancy Officer adds tenancy, arrangement, vacancy, change and concern rows. The SDA Manager adds notice rows, notice rule rows, home event rows and monthly review rows. The Tenancy Officer completes the service and review rights columns of a notice row, and opens a notice row for a participant's own notice. The Quality Manager adds the 3-monthly and 12-monthly review rows.
  2. Add a row within 2 business days of the event (our standard). Five rows are faster. Open a vacancy row within 1 business day of learning of the vacancy. Open a home event row within 1 business day. Open a concern row within 1 business day, when the concern is acknowledged. Open a notice rule row before the first notice of that kind. Enter a notice row before the notice is served.
  3. Use one row for each event. Where a record concerns several residents, columns AM, AO and AP hold one dated line for each person.
  4. Name participants by participant number. Name applicants by applicant number only. Never write an applicant's name in this register.
  5. Keep health details, diagnoses and behaviour support plan content out of the register. Put them on the participant's own file and give the file reference in column N.
  6. Never overwrite or delete an entry. A correction is a new version of the row, with the date, your name and the reason.
  7. A new SIL provider, or a change to who is responsible for a matter, is a new arrangement row. Set the old row to "superseded" on the same day.
  8. Nobody enters or approves a row about their own decision. The second approver in column AX is never the person who decided.
  9. When systems are down, write the record on paper. Enter the row within 2 business days of the system coming back.

A row is closed only when all of these are true:

  • every column required for its record type is filled
  • each action in column J is done, or sits in REG-QMS-01 Continuous Improvement Register with an owner and a due date
  • the participant was told the outcome, and column K shows the date and way
  • the SDA Manager has approved closing.

A tenancy row stays "current" until column W is filled. An arrangement row stays "current" until a new row supersedes it. A vacancy row closes when column AT is filled, or when the SDA Manager records that the place is withdrawn. A notice rule row stays "current" until the law changes and a new row supersedes it. A notice row closes when column BE shows the result. A change row closes when column BG or column BH is filled and the participant was told. A home event row closes when the action in column BM is done, or is tracked in REG-QMS-01. A concern row closes when column BR is filled and column BS shows where it went and how the person was told.
